to.name: Integrated IS-IS for IP and OSI

property: Integrated IS-IS directly reuses the OSI IS-IS link-state/SPF and Level 1/Level 2 routing architecture while adding IP-specific reachability/functions so one protocol can support IP, OSI, or dual environments.

date_or_range.notes: RFC publication representations; ISO 10589 chronology extends beyond these RFC dates.

sources.notes: Exact ISO edition mapping remains open.

sources.supports: explicit statement that Integrated IS-IS is based on OSI IS-IS with IP-specific functions added

negative_claims: This edge does not claim OSPF is an ancestor of Integrated IS-IS.
This edge does not imply OSI packet forwarding is encapsulated inside IP or vice versa; RFC 1195 forwards each protocol suite directly over lower-layer services.
This edge does not collapse ISO 10589 edition history into RFC 1142 metadata.
open_questions: Recover ISO 10589 revision chronology and early vendor implementations.
Identify first production IP deployments using Integrated IS-IS.
notes: A clear cross-standards-ecosystem derivation: an OSI link-state routing protocol is extended to become a major IP IGP lineage.
